colophon: Vēl Māṟal, compiled in grace by Vallimalai Srī Sacchidānanda Swāmigaḷ. ... The Vel-spear and the peacock are my refuge ...

lines.1: (... recite this line first, twelve times ...)
lines.2: The peerless one who rises in grace upon holy Thiruthani hill, the sage-elder who dwells within my heart, the wise lord who drives the peacock — the Vel of Guha!
lines.3: (... at the word "tiru" that ends every verse which follows, recite this entire line above in full ...)
lines.4: Full is her bosom, slender her waist, bright-gleaming her smile,
lines.5: dark her tresses, red her lips — the little huntress of the hill folk —
lines.6: and eyes unrivalled in their beauty.
lines.7: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.8: The peerless one who rises in grace upon holy Thiruthani hill,
lines.9: the sage-elder who dwells within my heart,
lines.10: the wise lord who drives the peacock — the Vel of Guha!
lines.11: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.12: For those who recite the Tiruppugazh, that hymn beyond all words,
lines.13: striking down the enemies who draw near,
lines.14: he brings forth the righteousness that melts the heart and rises within it.
lines.15: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.16: When he advances on the arrogant demon clans, their cunning withers like the poison-weed;
lines.17: the mighty, crowned Lord, bearer of power,
lines.18: whose valor is matched only by the ring of his warrior's anklets.
lines.19: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.20: The elephant-faced god of the broad, musth-streaming temples — Ganesha —
lines.21: at whose feet he too bows low,
lines.22: grants the boon that makes the battlefield burst into flower.
lines.23: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.24: Against the wrathful demons massed in defense at their many strongholds,
lines.25: their severed heads grinning, fangs bared,
lines.26: biting, eyes glaring, wailing — he strikes them down.
lines.27: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.28: For devotees who sing his praise, no calamity can ever touch them;
lines.29: for those who merely think of him, he roots out misfortune from their very lineage;
lines.30: he becomes my one true refuge.
lines.31: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.32: The hosts of his attendant spirits, gathered there, lost in joy,
lines.33: as if summoned by the curve of his lotus-soft hand —
lines.34: its very bend trembles with the call that gathers them.
lines.35: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.36: For the poet-scholar seated on the sweet, nectar-ripe bench of the Tamil Academy,
lines.37: melting at the music of his praise,
lines.38: he splits open the mountain cave and reveals the way through.
lines.39: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.40: Like the ancient thunderbolt that once clipped the wings of the mountains of every direction,
lines.41: as if newly sprung from their very peaks,
lines.42: his Vel flies on, thundering, swifter than flight itself.
lines.43: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.44: Brighter than the blazing sun, than the soft light of the waning moon,
lines.45: brighter than the radiance that fire itself holds back,
lines.46: he casts forth a splendor all his own.
lines.47: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.48: Even when I walk alone on a solitary path, one presence walks with me —
lines.49: close at my right, close on every side —
lines.50: he becomes my constant companion, by night and by day.
lines.51: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.52: The hungry demonesses of the battlefield wail and cry out in their hunger;
lines.53: as the asuras are cut down, their bodies bleeding,
lines.54: he graciously grants them flesh to feed upon.
lines.55: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.56: Breaking through the wave-tossed sea, its waters rushing in full spate,
lines.57: he drinks it down until its very banks burst open,
lines.58: then dams it, fills it with blood, and makes his sport there.
lines.59: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.60: For the celestials, for sages and the great, for Brahma who ordains destiny itself,
lines.61: for Hari (Vishnu) too, and for mortal men,
lines.62: he strikes down the afflicting karma that troubles even them.
lines.63: (... here, recite the full refrain above in full, at the word "tiru" ...)
lines.64: The bodies of the demons who come in treachery, their swollen, fattened entrails —
lines.66: these he gladly wears, delighted, twined into the crest of his hair.

lines.265: The red spear in the hand of the son of him who once mounted a chariot and burned the triple city [Shiva] — honed to so fine a point that Mount Krauncha itself crumbled, and the demons with it; the arrayed and encircling battle-ranks were broken, Soorapadman himself writhing in defeat — his great host destroyed, and so the realm of Indra was saved.
lines.266: The heroic Vel, the streaming Vel that freed the celestials from their captivity, the resolute Vel, the sacred hand-held Vel of the radiant red Lord — the Vel that plunged into the ocean, the victorious Vel, the Vel that pierced through both Soorapadman's chest and the mountain — that Vel alone is my refuge.
lines.267: ... ... ... the Vel-spear and the peacock are my refuge ... ... ...
